## What changed on run 4 — 2026-10-30

One thing moved upstream since run 3, and it is the finding run 3 opened and could not close.

### `docs/adr/0004` — the module of a `*.NotFound` code names the aggregate that was not found

Accepted 2026-10-30, project-wide. It fills a gap ADR-0003 left open and supersedes no clause of it.
Run 3 had merged `Category.GroupNotFound` into `CategoryGroup.NotFound` and written the principle
into the `Error` schema as a statement about that one pair; ADR-0004 promotes it to the rule and
applies it everywhere.

Four codes changed, 27 become 25:

| was | is | why |
|---|---|---|
| `Transaction.AccountNotFound` | `Account.NotFound` | merged — one refusal had two codes |
| `Transaction.CategoryNotFound` | `Category.NotFound` | merged — one refusal had two codes |
| `Transfer.SourceAccountNotFound` | `Account.SourceNotFound` | renamed — the role stays, the module moves |
| `Transfer.DestinationAccountNotFound` | `Account.DestinationNotFound` | renamed — same |

The role qualifier is the ADR's one clause on top of the plain rule: it survives only where one
request can fail to find the same aggregate twice, which in this contract is the transfer pair and
nothing else. `setCategoryGroup` still tells its two `404`s apart — `Category.NotFound` for the
entry being moved, `CategoryGroup.NotFound` for the target group.

`csv-import` moved in the same change: `Import.AccountNotFound` → `Account.NotFound`,
`MappingProfile.CategoryNotFound` → `Category.NotFound`, `Import.RunNotFound` → `Import.NotFound`.
So the two shared codes are literally one code each, and the repository carries one convention.
`CLAUDE.md` §API, `.claude/rules/openapi.md` §7 and the skill's `references/error-catalog.md` were
amended in the same change — the last one because it is what a **first** run on a new feature reads.

**Nothing else moved.** No operation, schema, field, bound, status or path changed. `PRD.md`,
`sad.md` and `data-model.md` are unchanged since run 2, so the shape of the surface is the same 21
operations over the same 33 schemas. `info.version` stays `0.1.0` — nothing has shipped against it.

## What changed on run 3 — 2026-10-22

Three things moved upstream since run 2. None of them touched `PRD.md`, `sad.md` §5/§6 or
`data-model.md`, so the *shape* of the surface is unchanged: the same 21 operations over the same
33 schemas.

### 1. `docs/adr/0003` — every code is `Module.ErrorName` in PascalCase

Accepted 2026-10-22, project-wide. It supersedes the **spelling clause** of ADR-0002 and nothing
else: the flat envelope, the status classes and the "a finished batch is a success" rule all stand.
`CLAUDE.md` §API, `.claude/rules/openapi.md` (new deviation §7) and `core-ledger/sad.md` §8 were
amended in the same change.

The 28 codes were re-spelled by hand in the previous commit. **This run verified that work rather
than redoing it.** All 28 strings were extracted from `openapi.yaml` and compared one by one against
the "becomes" column of the ADR's mapping table:

- **28 of 28 matched exactly.** No code was missed, none was mis-cased, none changed meaning,
  status or operation.
- All 28 match the new `Error.code` pattern `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`.
- **No snake_case code is left anywhere in the document** — not in a value, not in an `example`, not
  in a `description`.

One straggler was found and fixed: the `MoneyAmount` schema description still said a bad amount is
refused with `*.amount_not_positive`. It now names `Transaction.AmountNotPositive` and
`Transfer.AmountNotPositive`. Prose is where a re-spelling hides, because no grep over `code:` finds
it.

### 2. `Category.GroupNotFound` is merged into `CategoryGroup.NotFound`

ADR-0003 surfaced this and deliberately left it to this run. **It is merged.** The reasoning is in
Section B.2 under *Decision — the duplicate "group not found" refusal*. 28 codes become 27.

### 3. The report format — Section A is now one tree per operation

Run 2's Section A was a flat table, one row per dotted path, grouped by schema. The skill's template
now asks for **one tree per operation**, with the C# record and property names the endpoint folder
will hold, the contract type on every node, a `conf` column, and the origin on the row it belongs
to. Converting it is the bulk of this run; what the conversion changed is in Section A's preamble.

### What a reconcile is really for, and what it found

The load-bearing half of `--reconcile` is not re-deriving — it is finding a field whose origin now
**disagrees** with the model. Stated plainly so the absence is not read as a skipped check:

- **No field changed its origin.** Scenario was already A at run 2, so there was no inferred origin
  to promote and none found in disagreement with a column.
- **No type was loosened or tightened.** Every bound in Section B.3 still matches its column.
- **Nothing parked at run 2 is now closed**, and one new finding was opened — the `*.NotFound`
  module convention, Section B.2.

### Lint repairs made before this report was written

`references/openapi-lint.md` is the only gate the document gets until `./build.sh check` exists.
Three of its checks were failing at run 2 and are fixed here. They are recorded rather than hidden,
because a check that silently started passing teaches nothing:

| check | was | now |
|---|---|---|
| First line is the `REFERENCE SPEC` comment | missing — the file opened with "Derived by …", so a reader finding it alone could mistake it for `/openapi/v1.json` | added |
| `Presentation/Endpoints/<Resource>/<Operation>/` in every `description` | **0 of 21 operations** had it | all 21, taken from the `sad.md` §5 Presentation tree — not invented |
| Skill name and deviation count in the header | `sdlc:api-forge`, "the five FinNavis deviations" | `finnavis-api-forge`, "the seven" — `.claude/rules/openapi.md` now has seven |

## Section A — field origins

One tree per operation. Names are the **C# records and properties** the operation folder will hold
(`CategoryGroupId`), because this section is read by whoever writes
`Presentation/Endpoints/<Resource>/<Operation>/`; the wire keys stay snake_case in `openapi.yaml`
and the mapping is mechanical. Types are the **contract's**, not C#'s — `string` for money, never
`decimal`, because drift point 3 checks the contract type against the column. `?` marks the 3.1
union `type: [x, "null"]`. `conf` is **high** for a typed column, **med** for an acceptance
criterion or a named convention, **low** for an inference (none here — this is scenario A).

The origin sits on the row it belongs to and wraps under itself, with the tree guide in front, so a
reviewer reads a claim and its source without moving their eyes off the line. Nothing is pushed into
a footnote and nothing is shortened.

A `$ref`'d schema is expanded **once**, under the first operation that carries it; later uses name
the type and point back (`see createCategory`).

**One C# record per operation folder, even when two serialise identically** (`CLAUDE.md` §API). So
`CreateAccountResponse` and `RenameAccountResponse` are two records over one `Account` schema. The
`$ref` keeps the document from drifting against itself; the separate records keep one operation's
change from reshaping another endpoint (`.claude/rules/openapi.md` §4).

**What the conversion from run 2's table changed.** No origin was dropped, weakened or invented —
every claim in run 2's 60-odd rows is still here. Three things are visible that the flat table hid:

1. **Nesting.** `Breakdown.Expense.Groups[].Categories[].Total` was four unrelated rows; it is now
   one indented path whose element types (`BreakdownSide`, `BreakdownGroup`, `BreakdownCategory`)
   sit on the nodes. The same for `HistoryPage.Items[]` and its two member types.
2. **Which operation carries which field.** Run 2 grouped by schema, so `Account` appeared once and
   the reader had to find the four operations using it. Each operation now shows its own request and
   response.
3. **The `*` rows are gone.** Run 2 collapsed whole request bodies into `RecordTransactionRequest.*`
   and `EditTransferRequest.*`. Every property is written out.

### `createAccount` — `POST /api/v1/accounts`

```text
request  CreateAccountRequest
└─ Name                   string(1..100) high ← accounts.name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL UNIQUE. maxLength copies the
                                                column; minLength 1 is a tightening this contract adds, because NOT
                                                NULL does not forbid an empty string and AC-07 reads a name as what
                                                identifies an account

response 201  Account                                      (record CreateAccountResponse)
├─ Id                     uuid           high ← accounts.id. UUID v7 minted in the Application layer with
│                                               Guid.CreateVersion7() — ADR-0005
├─ Name                   string(100)    high ← accounts.name
└─ CreatedAt              date-time      high ← accounts.created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
```

### `getAccountBalances` — `GET /api/v1/accounts/balances`

```text
query
└─ AccountId              uuid?            med  ← an optional filter naming one accounts.id. AC-14 reads one
                                                  account or all of them, so the parameter belongs to the operation
                                                  rather than to a column

response 200  AccountBalances
├─ Accounts[]             AccountBalance[] high ← one entry per accounts row. Not a cursor page: sad.md §6 flow 7
│                                                 reads every account in one query, and data-model.md records that
│                                                 accounts holds a handful of rows
│  ├─ AccountId           uuid             high ← accounts.id
│  ├─ Name                string(100)      high ← accounts.name
│  └─ Balance             string           high ← computed at read time and never stored (ADR-0002) — the sum of
│                                                 every transaction and transfer naming the account, AC-14. A
│                                                 string on the wire and decimal in C# (rules §2); signed, because
│                                                 a computed balance can be below zero
└─ Total                  string           high ← the per-account figures added together, sad.md §6 flow 7. AC-15 —
                                                  a transfer between the owner's own accounts leaves this unchanged
```

### `recordTransaction` — `POST /api/v1/transactions`

```text
request  RecordTransactionRequest
├─ AccountId              uuid         high ← transactions.account_id UUID NOT NULL, FK to accounts(id). Exactly
│                                             one account — a movement touching two is a transfer (sad.md §12)
├─ CategoryId             uuid         high ← transactions.category_id UUID NOT NULL, FK to categories(id). AC-01,
│                                             AC-03 — every transaction names exactly one category
├─ Amount                 string       high ← transactions.amount NUMERIC(19,4) NOT NULL. A string on the wire
│                                             (rules §2): a JSON number is an IEEE double in most clients and would
│                                             lose the fourth decimal. Always positive — direction comes from the
│                                             category's kind, data-model.md decision 3
├─ OccurredOn             date         high ← transactions.occurred_on DATE NOT NULL — a calendar day with no time
│                                             and no timezone, so a late-evening entry cannot slide into the next
│                                             period (decision 1)
└─ Note                   string(500)? high ← transactions.note VARCHAR(500) NULL (decision 2). Optional free text,
                                              stored and returned as plain text and never interpreted (PRD §6.1)

response 201  Transaction                                  (record RecordTransactionResponse)
├─ Id                     uuid         high ← transactions.id, UUID v7 — time-ordered, which is what makes it a
│                                             stable tiebreaker when paging history by date (ADR-0005, sad.md §11)
├─ AccountId              uuid         high ← transactions.account_id
├─ CategoryId             uuid         high ← transactions.category_id
├─ Amount                 string       high ← transactions.amount
├─ OccurredOn             date         high ← transactions.occurred_on
├─ Note                   string(500)? high ← transactions.note. AC-01 — the note is kept with the entry
└─ CreatedAt              date-time    high ← transactions.created_at
```

### `getHistory` — `GET /api/v1/history`

```text
query
├─ From                      date?         med  ← first calendar day of the period, inclusive. AC-16; matched
│                                                 against transactions.occurred_on and transfers.occurred_on,
│                                                 served by idx_transactions_occurred_on_account_id and
│                                                 idx_transfers_occurred_on
├─ To                        date?         med  ← last calendar day of the period, inclusive. The same columns and
│                                                 indexes
├─ AccountId                 uuid?         med  ← AC-16. For a transfer that means either side — both FK columns
│                                                 carry their own index
├─ CategoryId                uuid?         med  ← AC-16. Setting it excludes every transfer, because a transfer
│                                                 carries no category_id and can never match. Settled at the api-
│                                                 forge gate in run 1; sad.md §6 flow 8 flagged it and the PRD does
│                                                 not state it
├─ After                     string(200)?  med  ← opaque keyset cursor over (occurred_on, id) — rules §3 and
│                                                 ADR-0001. History is a UNION ALL of two tables, so a bare id
│                                                 cannot locate a page boundary. The server mints the token and the
│                                                 client passes it back unread
├─ Before                    string(200)?  med  ← the same, backwards. Present because the baseline's `before` is
│                                                 unusable without a prev_cursor — rules §3
└─ Limit                     int(1..200)   med  ← default 50, settled at the api-forge gate in run 1. PRD §6
                                                  budgets p95 ≤ 400 ms per page over ~20 000 movements, and ~550
                                                  movements a month means the default pulls a month in about eleven
                                                  requests

response 200  HistoryPage                                  (record GetHistoryResponse)
├─ Items[]                   HistoryItem[] high ← oneOf HistoryTransaction | HistoryTransfer, discriminated on
│                                                 Kind. AC-16 — each row is marked as one or the other. An empty
│                                                 array is a normal answer, not a failure (AC-17)
│  ├─ Kind                   const(2)      med  ← the discriminator, the literal "transaction" or "transfer". AC-16
│  │                                              and ADR-0001 — it is not a column, because the two live in
│  │                                              separate tables
│  ├─ Id                     uuid          high ← transactions.id or transfers.id — the tiebreaker inside one day,
│  │                                              UUID v7 (ADR-0005)
│  ├─ OccurredOn             date          high ← transactions.occurred_on or transfers.occurred_on — the leading
│  │                                              key of the page order
│  ├─ Amount                 string        high ← transactions.amount or transfers.amount NUMERIC(19,4), a string
│  │                                              on the wire (rules §2)
│  ├─ AccountId              uuid          high ← transactions.account_id — on a transaction row only
│  ├─ AccountName            string(100)   high ← accounts.name, joined in so a client needs no second request per
│  │                                              row
│  ├─ CategoryId             uuid          high ← transactions.category_id — on a transaction row only
│  ├─ CategoryName           string(100)   high ← categories.name, joined in
│  ├─ CategoryKind           enum(2)       high ← categories.kind — it carries the direction, since amount is
│  │                                              always positive (data-model.md decision 3)
│  ├─ Note                   string(500)?  high ← transactions.note. AC-16 — each transaction shows its note
│  ├─ SourceAccountId        uuid          high ← transfers.source_account_id — on a transfer row only
│  ├─ SourceAccountName      string(100)   high ← accounts.name, joined
│  ├─ DestinationAccountId   uuid          high ← transfers.destination_account_id — on a transfer row only
│  ├─ DestinationAccountName string(100)   high ← accounts.name, joined a second time
│  └─ CreatedAt              date-time     high ← transactions.created_at or transfers.created_at
├─ HasNext                   bool          med  ← page wrapper, rules §3
├─ HasPrev                   bool          med  ← page wrapper, rules §3
├─ NextCursor                string(200)?  med  ← pass back as `after` to read the next page; null on the last
│                                                 page. Opaque — a client never builds one
└─ PrevCursor                string(200)?  med  ← pass back as `before` to read the previous page; null on the
                                                  first page. Added to the baseline wrapper, rules §3
```

### `getBreakdown` — `GET /api/v1/reports/breakdown`

```text
query
├─ From                   date                high ← required. transactions.occurred_on, served by
│                                                    idx_transactions_occurred_on_account_id — AC-18
├─ To                     date                high ← required. The same column and index
└─ AccountId              uuid?               med  ← optional. PRD §1 asks for a period- and account-filtered
                                                     breakdown; the second column of that same index

response 200  Breakdown                                    (record GetBreakdownResponse)
├─ Period                 BreakdownPeriod     high ← the period the answer covers, echoed back
│  ├─ From                date                high ← the From query parameter
│  └─ To                  date                high ← the To query parameter
├─ AccountId              uuid?               med  ← the account filter that produced this answer, or null for
│                                                    every account
├─ Expense                BreakdownSide       high ← AC-18 — spending, kept apart from earning. Only categories
│                                                    whose kind is Expense
│  ├─ Total               string              high ← AC-19 — the period total for this side. The groups below,
│  │                                                 Default group included, add up to it
│  └─ Groups[]            BreakdownGroup[]    high ← AC-18 — totals per group, resolved against the current
│                                                    category-to-group mapping at query time (ADR-0002)
│     ├─ CategoryGroupId  uuid?               high ← category_groups.id. null is the Default group bucket —
│     │                                              produced by this report and never a row (sad.md §12)
│     ├─ Name             string(100)         high ← category_groups.name, or the literal "Default group" when the
│     │                                              id is null
│     ├─ Total            string              high ← the sum of the categories below, over transactions.amount
│     └─ Categories[]     BreakdownCategory[] high ← AC-18 — totals per category
│        ├─ CategoryId    uuid                high ← categories.id
│        ├─ Name          string(100)         high ← categories.name
│        └─ Total         string              high ← AC-13 — this figure for a closed period does not change when
│                                                    the category is moved between groups, because a transaction
│                                                    names its category and never its group
└─ Income                 BreakdownSide       high ← AC-18 — earning. The same shape as Expense. No transfer is
                                                     counted on either side: the query reads transactions and never
                                                     touches transfers, so AC-20 holds structurally (ADR-0001,
                                                     sad.md §6 flow 3)
```

### Error envelope — every `4xx` and the one `500`

```text
Error                                                      (docs/adr/0002 — flat, NOT Problem Details)
├─ Code                   string  high ← pattern ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ — Module.ErrorName in
│                                        PascalCase, docs/adr/0003. The only part a client branches on, and the one
│                                        PascalCase value in the body
├─ Message                string  high ← the refusal sentence the owner reads, lifted from the PRD acceptance
│                                        criterion the refusal implements and never invented here (sad.md §8, Error
│                                        handling)
└─ Details                object? med  ← optional structured context: the failing fields, a conflicting id, a
                                         count. Every key inside it stays snake_case — see the table below
```


### What rides in `details`, per code

Optional, omitted rather than sent empty. Every key inside it stays snake_case — the `code` is the
one PascalCase value in the body (`docs/adr/0003`).

| code | `details` keys | why the client needs them |
|---|---|---|
| `Account.HasRecordedHistory` | `transaction_count`, `transfer_count` | AC-09 — the owner is told recorded history depends on the account; the counts say how much |
| `Category.HasRecordedHistory` | `transaction_count` | AC-12, the same shape. A category is named by transactions only |
| `Category.GroupKindMismatch` | `category_kind`, `category_group_kind` | AC-30 — the two sides that failed to match, so the client can say which is which |
| `Transaction.KindChangeNotAllowed` | `rejected_property` | AC-24 — names the property that would have turned the entry into a transfer |
| `Transfer.CategoryNotAllowed` | `rejected_property` | AC-23 — the same shape, for the property a transfer has no column for |
| `Category.NotFound` | `category_id` | AC-03 — the unknown category is named back to the owner |
| `History.InvalidFilter` | `from`, `to` | the two values that contradict each other |
| `Breakdown.InvalidPeriod` | `from`, `to` | the same |

## Section B — drift findings (6-point checklist)

### 1. Operation ↔ data model *(core)* — ✓

Every leaf in the Section A trees maps to a column, with the type and the nullability that column
has. No leaf disagrees with its column.

Nine leaves are **not** columns. Each has a named origin rather than a missing one, which is what
this point asks for:

- `AccountBalance.Balance` and `AccountBalances.Total` — computed at read time. ADR-0002 removed
  every stored balance, so there is no column to point at and that is the design, not a gap.
- `HistoryItem.Kind` — the discriminator. ADR-0001 keeps transactions and transfers in separate
  tables, so no column carries it; the query supplies the literal.
- `HistoryTransaction.AccountName`, `.CategoryName`, `HistoryTransfer.SourceAccountName`,
  `.DestinationAccountName` — joined from `accounts.name` and `categories.name` so a client needs no
  second request per row. The bound is copied from the column they are joined from.
- `HistoryPage.HasNext` / `.HasPrev` / `.NextCursor` / `.PrevCursor` and `getHistory.Limit` — the
  cursor page wrapper, `.claude/rules/openapi.md` §3.
- `BreakdownSide.Total`, `BreakdownGroup.Total`, `BreakdownCategory.Total` — aggregates over
  `transactions.amount`, carrying its `NUMERIC(19,4)` precision.
- `BreakdownGroup.Name` when `CategoryGroupId` is `null` — the literal `Default group`. It is
  produced by the report and is never a row (`sad.md` §12, `GLOSSARY.md`).

**Deliberately not surfaced**, recorded rather than silently omitted:

| column | why | action |
|---|---|---|
| `transactions.external_ref` | ADR-0006: *"Always null in this feature. csv-import and message capture fill it later."* Exposing it would advertise a field that is always `null`; accepting it would let a client set something this feature does not support | **Intentionally internal** — accept as is. `csv-import` surfaces it |

Nine modules are in use across the repository; this contract uses seven of them — `Account`,
`Breakdown`, `Category`, `CategoryGroup`, `History`, `Transaction`, `Transfer`. `Import` and
`MappingProfile` belong to `csv-import`. `.claude/rules/openapi.md` §7 lists all nine, so `History`
and `Breakdown` are blessed modules even though they are not aggregates in `GLOSSARY.md`.

**No collision with `csv-import`.** Its 12 codes, 6 `operationId`s and 6 paths were read this run
and share nothing with these 27, these 21 and these 11.

#### Decision — the duplicate "group not found" refusal

`docs/adr/0003` surfaced this and explicitly handed it to this run:

| before | used by |
|---|---|
| `Category.GroupNotFound` | `createCategory`, `setCategoryGroup` |
| `CategoryGroup.NotFound` | `listCategories`, `renameCategoryGroup`, `deleteCategoryGroup` |

Both carried the identical message — *"No category group in the ledger has id …"* — both returned
`404`, and both meant the same thing.

**Decided: merge them. `CategoryGroup.NotFound` survives; `Category.GroupNotFound` is gone.**
27 codes, not 28. Four reasons, in the order they carried weight:

1. **It is one refusal.** Same cause, same status, same sentence the owner reads. A client cannot
   act differently on the two, so the second code is a branch that exists only to be forgotten —
   which is exactly what `.claude/rules/openapi.md` forbids: *one `code` in the contract equals one
   definition in the repo*.
2. **The split was not even applied consistently.** `listCategories` names a group through a
   *filter* — a reference, the same kind of reference `createCategory` makes — and it already
   returned `CategoryGroup.NotFound`. So the two codes did not divide the sites by any rule; they
   divided them by accident.
3. **Nothing is lost at any of the five sites.** The only operation that can refuse two different
   things with a `404` is `setCategoryGroup`, and after the merge its two refusals are told apart by
   the **module** — `Category.NotFound` for the entry being moved, `CategoryGroup.NotFound` for the
   target. That reads better than the prefix-inside-the-name it replaces.
4. **The registry lands cleanly.** `CategoryGroupErrors.NotFound` is one constant instead of
   `CategoryErrors.GroupNotFound` and `CategoryGroupErrors.NotFound` returning two strings for one
   event. Nothing parses these strings yet, so the merge costs one contract edit and no migration.

What it cost, recorded honestly: it departs from the `<Entity>.<Ref>NotFound` derivation that
`references/error-catalog.md` gives for a foreign key. That derivation still holds where it adds
information — `Transfer.SourceAccountNotFound` against `Transfer.DestinationAccountNotFound` is the
case it was written for. The principle this merge picks is narrower and is written into the `Error`
schema: **the module names the aggregate that was not found, not the aggregate the request was
operating on.**

Four of the five sites now `$ref` `#/components/responses/CategoryGroupNotFound`. The fifth,
`setCategoryGroup`, is written out because its `404` carries two examples; the error *schema* is
still a single `$ref`, so no shape is duplicated.

#### Opened on run 3, closed on run 4 — the same shape, in six more codes, across two features

Checking the merge turned up that `docs/adr/0003`'s closing claim — *"No other pair collides"* — was
too narrow. Six codes carried one of two identical messages:

| the one refusal | codes that advertised it |
|---|---|
| *"No account in the ledger has id …"* | `Account.NotFound`, `Transaction.AccountNotFound`, `Transfer.SourceAccountNotFound`, `Transfer.DestinationAccountNotFound` |
| *"No category in the ledger has id …"* | `Category.NotFound`, `Transaction.CategoryNotFound` |

Run 3 parked it, because none of the three obstacles was a contract edit's to remove: the transfer
pair cannot merge without deciding where "which side" goes; two of the codes were the worked
examples in a rules file and a skill reference; and `csv-import` had the same shape, so deciding it
in one feature would put two conventions in the repository.

**Closed on run 4 by `docs/adr/0004`.** The module is the aggregate that was not found, and the
error name carries a role qualifier only when one request can miss the same aggregate twice. That
answers all three obstacles in one rule: the transfer pair becomes `Account.SourceNotFound` and
`Account.DestinationNotFound` with the role in the code and nothing in `details`; the rules file and
the skill reference were amended by the ADR, which is an ADR's job; and both contracts moved in the
same change. The six codes are now three: `Account.NotFound`, `Account.SourceNotFound`,
`Account.DestinationNotFound` for accounts, and `Category.NotFound` for categories.

Parked in Section D with the next step. The group pair was a defect inside one aggregate pair; this
one is a convention question across two features, and it deserves its own record.

Every bound in the contract was copied from `data-model.md`, not chosen. Re-checked this run,
column by column:

| contract | data-model.md | match |
|---|---|---|

| `note` `maxLength: 500` | `transactions.note` VARCHAR(500) (decision 2) | ✓ |
| `MoneyAmount` `^\d{1,15}(\.\d{1,4})?$` | `NUMERIC(19,4)` — 19 digits, scale 4, so 15 before the point | ✓ |
| `SignedMoneyAmount` `^-?\d{1,15}(\.\d{1,4})?$` | the same precision; the sign is for a computed balance (ADR-0002) | ✓ |
| `occurred_on` `format: date` | `occurred_on` DATE (decision 1 — no time, no timezone) | ✓ |
| `created_at` `format: date-time` | `created_at` TIMESTAMPTZ | ✓ |
| `category_group_id` `type: [string, "null"]` | `categories.category_group_id` UUID NULL | ✓ |
| `account_id`, `category_id` required | both FK NOT NULL | ✓ |
| `409 Account.DuplicateName` | `accounts.name` UNIQUE (decision 4) | ✓ |
| `409 Category.DuplicateName` | `categories` UNIQUE (`name`, `kind`) (decision 4) | ✓ |
| `409 CategoryGroup.DuplicateName` | `category_groups` UNIQUE (`name`, `kind`) (decision 4) | ✓ |
| `409 Category.GroupKindMismatch` | **no constraint by design** — decision 7 keeps AC-30 a domain invariant | ✓ |
| `Error.code` pattern `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$` | not a column — `docs/adr/0003` and `.claude/rules/openapi.md` §7 | ✓ |

**No bound is looser than its column**, which is the failure this point exists to catch — the
database would then reject what the contract accepts.

**One bound is stricter than its column, deliberately.** Every `name` carries `minLength: 1`, which
`data-model.md` does not have: `NOT NULL` does not forbid an empty string. It is marked `high` in
Section A because the column fixes the upper bound, but the lower bound is the contract's own
addition, and it is named here so a reviewer does not read it as copied.

Two rules the schema deliberately does **not** hold, unchanged from run 2 and re-verified:

- `amount > 0` (AC-02) is not a schema constraint. A regex cannot cleanly reject `0.0000`, and
  decision 6 puts the rule in the Domain entity rather than in a `CHECK`. The contract documents it
  on `MoneyAmount` and returns `Transaction.AmountNotPositive` or `Transfer.AmountNotPositive`.
- "a group and its categories share a side" (AC-30) is not a schema constraint either. Decision 7
  considered a composite FK and rejected it — a unique index no query reads, and a frozen `kind`.
  The contract returns `409 Category.GroupKindMismatch` with both sides in `details`.

In both cases the model and the contract agree about *where* the rule lives, which is what this
point checks. **No PRD §5 ↔ `data-model.md` contradiction was found**, so the "take the stricter
value" rule did not fire.

### 6. Contract ↔ the served document *(supporting, FinNavis)* — N/A

**N/A — there is nothing to diff against.** `src/FinNavis.Presentation/Endpoints/` holds a single
`.gitkeep` and no endpoint folder. The whole of `src/` holds four C# files: three `AssemblyMarker.cs`
and `Program.cs`. No ASP.NET Core document is generated at `/openapi/v1.json` because no Minimal API
endpoint is mapped.

Stated as N/A rather than ✓ on purpose. Marking an unchecked point ✓ is the failure this point
exists to prevent. It is checked at `implement-tasks`, when the four sub-checks become answerable:

1. every operation here has its `Presentation/Endpoints/<Resource>/<Operation>/` folder — the 21
   folder names are now in the contract, so this is a comparison and not a re-derivation;
2. paths, methods and status codes match;
3. no endpoint exists in the code that this contract never declared;
4. **the error shape the code returns is the flat envelope, not `application/problem+json`.** This
   is the one that will break by default: ASP.NET Core answers with `problem+json` for routing 404s,
   model-binding failures, `Results.ValidationProblem` and anything under `AddProblemDetails`. That
   default has to be turned off and every failure routed through the one envelope, or the API
   answers with two shapes and a client switching on `code` breaks on exactly the requests that
   never reached a handler (`docs/adr/0002`, `CLAUDE.md` §API).

to tighten on types.

## Section D — Deferrals

| what | why parked | next step |
|---|---|---|
| **No error registry in the repo** (point 2) | `src/` is a skeleton; there is nothing to check the 25 codes against | `implement-tasks` creates the registry from the table in point 2, one class per module. Then `--reconcile` verifies it |
| **Five groups / nine responses with no §6 branch** (point 5) | Four are parameter-shape validation a sequence diagram legitimately omits. One is a real gap | `/finnavis-complete-sequence-diagrams core-ledger --flow "record a transfer"` — flow 2 loads both accounts but draws no not-found branch. Low urgency |
| **Contract ↔ served document not checkable** (point 6) | No endpoint exists yet | `implement-tasks`. The 21 endpoint folders are now written into the contract, so the diff is mechanical |
| **Two PRD §8 open questions on group reporting** | Both are response-shape questions due at this gate. The contract follows the PRD's own stated default rather than deciding for the owner | (a) An empty group in the breakdown: **left out** — `BreakdownGroup` is unchanged, so a group with no categories produces no row. (b) How many categories a group removal affected: **not reported** — `deleteCategoryGroup` returns `204` with no body. Flip either and `--reconcile` |
| **`spectral lint` is not wired** | The repo has no `check` target (`CLAUDE.md` "Not set up yet") | Add `spectral lint docs/features/*/contracts/openapi.yaml` to `build.sh` when CI is stood up. PRD §6 already schedules the harness as a prerequisite task |

**Closed since run 3:**

- **The `*.NotFound` module convention** — settled 2026-10-30 by
  `docs/adr/0004-name-the-not-found-aggregate-in-the-module.md`, applied to both contracts in one
  change. It was the one finding run 3 opened and could not close. Details in point 2.

**Accepted as is (no action, reason recorded):**

- **`Category.GroupNotFound` is gone and `CategoryGroup.NotFound` is used at five sites** — decided
  on this run, reasoning in point 2. The departure from the `<Entity>.<Ref>NotFound` derivation is
  deliberate and is written into the `Error` schema description so the next reader meets it there.
- **`setCategoryGroup` writes its `404` out instead of `$ref`-ing the shared response** — it is the
  only operation whose `404` carries two different refusals. The error *schema* is still one `$ref`,
  so nothing is duplicated.
- `transactions.external_ref` is not surfaced — **intentionally internal** per ADR-0006 (*"Always
  null in this feature"*). `csv-import` surfaces it.
- **No `securitySchemes`, `security: []` globally, no `401` and no `403`** — PRD §3, PRD §6.1,
  `sad.md` §8 and `sad.md` §11 all state there is no sign-in and no second actor. Deviation 1 in
  `.claude/rules/openapi.md`. The OAuth feature flips it back and every contract is re-run.
- **No `Idempotency-Key` on any mutating endpoint, and no `contracts/events.md`** — `sad.md` §6
  states it outright: *"No flow in this feature is asynchronous."* §8 confirms: *"Outbox / events:
  N/A — one process, no module-to-module messaging."*
- **No plain "list accounts" operation** — `getAccountBalances` covers AC-07's "appears in the
  account list".
- **Money crosses the wire as a `string`** — deviation 2. A JSON number is an IEEE double in most
  clients and loses the fourth decimal place of `NUMERIC(19,4)`.
- **`prev_cursor` is in the page wrapper** although the baseline wrapper has only `next_cursor` —
  the baseline's own `before` parameter is unusable without it. Deviation 3.
- **Examples carry placeholder data only** — `Test Account`, `Test Savings`, `Test Groceries`,
  `Test Utilities`, `Test Salary`, `Test note`, and invented amounts. No real merchant, amount or
  account is anywhere in this document (`CLAUDE.md` Safety).

## Decisions settled at this gate

### Run 4 — 2026-10-30

0. **Does the module of a `*.NotFound` code name the aggregate that was not found, or the aggregate
   the request was operating on?** Source: Section D, the one finding run 3 opened and could not
   close.
   → **The aggregate that was not found**, settled project-wide by `docs/adr/0004`. The error name
   carries a role qualifier only when one request can miss the same aggregate twice, which keeps
   the transfer pair distinguishable without overloading `details`. Four codes changed here, three
   in `csv-import`, and both contracts moved in the same change.

### Run 3 — 2026-10-22

1. **Do `Category.GroupNotFound` and `CategoryGroup.NotFound` describe one refusal, and if so which
   one survives?** Source: `docs/adr/0003`, section *"A finding this record surfaced but does not
   resolve"*, which handed it here by name.
   → **Yes, one refusal. `CategoryGroup.NotFound` survives and is used at all five sites.** Same
   cause, same status, same sentence, and the split was never applied consistently — `listCategories`
   already used `CategoryGroup.NotFound` for the same kind of reference `createCategory` made.
   Nothing is lost: at the one operation that can refuse two things, the module tells them apart.
   Full reasoning in Section B.2.

2. **Is the ADR-0003 re-spelling complete?** Not an open question the sources raised, but the thing
   this run was asked to verify.
   → **Yes — 28 of 28 codes matched the ADR's mapping exactly**, and the one straggler was in prose,
   not in a code value: `MoneyAmount`'s description still named `*.amount_not_positive`. Fixed.

### Runs 1 and 2 — recorded, still standing

3. **History page size.** Source: `sad.md` §6 *"History paging is drawn but never specified"* and
   `data-model.md` Open items.
   → **`limit`: minimum 1, maximum 200, default 50.** PRD §6 budgets p95 ≤ 400 ms per page over
   ~20 000 movements; at ~550 movements a month the default pulls a month in about eleven requests.

4. **Does a category filter on history exclude transfers?** Source: `sad.md` §6 *"AC-16 pulls in two
   directions here… confirm it at `/sdlc-api-forge`"*.
   → **Yes.** A transfer carries no `category_id`, so it can never match the filter; returning it
   anyway would mean the result did not all match what was asked. Written on the `category_id`
   parameter of `getHistory`.

5. **Paging style for the `UNION ALL` history.** Source: `sad.md` §11.
   → **Cursor, keyset over `(occurred_on, id)`.** `id` is a time-ordered UUID v7 (ADR-0005), which
   `data-model.md` already names as the tiebreaker. The cursor is an opaque string rather than a
   bare UUID, because one id cannot locate a boundary across two tables — deviation 3.

1. **Whether `src/` gained an error registry**, so drift point 2 moves from deferred to checked, and
   whether `src/FinNavis.Presentation/Endpoints/` gained folders, so point 6 moves from N/A to
   checked. Both are `implement-tasks`' job.
2. **Whether flow 2 gained a not-found branch**, so the last real point-5 gap closes. The other four
   are parameter-shape validation and stay deferred.
3. **Whether either PRD §8 group-reporting question was answered differently** from the default the
   contract follows — an empty group left out of the breakdown, and a `204` with no body on group
   removal. Both are one-line contract changes if the answer flips.
